that they are going to
create large reflections

but the most common
objection to 90-degree traces

due to an impedance discontinuity.

oriented like this as a 90-degree route,

and I send in some signal

propagating in this direction,

what happens when it reaches
this region of the trace?

when this signal
encounters this dashed area here,

right at this corner of
this 90-degree trace?
Well, the myth basically says

that because Z in free
space is very large,

we would expect that we
get a large reflection
equal to basically Z,
we'll call it f,
minus Z0 divided by Zf plus Z0.

that would basically take
this reflection coefficient to one.
So this is what the myth says,

that we get this huge reflection
right here at this edge,
right here at this 90-degree trace.

Now, this is what's really
interesting about this myth

will happen in 90-degree traces,
but they never bring up vias.

a form of a right-angle
bend for routing in PCBs,

and nobody ever brings up
this huge reflection in vias,
even though it is also a right-angle turn.

So why do people bring up this
very basic misunderstanding

about signal propagation along
these right-angle traces?
Well, it comes from this idea

that signals propagating
along a trace and a PCB

are basically like bunches of
water flowing through a pipe.

that frankly folks like myself use

to teach electricity to
101-level students in university,

which helps to understand how
current flows in conductors.

not physically accurate,
but it is very conceptually useful
for understanding Kirchhoff's current law.
Now, we need to get away from that

when actually looking at how
signals propagate on a PCB,

because the reality is
that signals on a PCB
do not propagate like this
and then reach a discontinuity

and then experience a big
reflection as shown here.
They actually exist in the space
between the conductor and the ground plane
in the dielectric that makes up your PCB.

So this is not a
physically accurate picture

because it's based on a
physically inaccurate description
of how current flows.

not physically accurate,

into the 56-gigabits NRZ signals,

impact of the corner to be.

you know, 50m narrow line,

what's gonna be the
impact of the capacity,
the capacitors on the corner?"

more important problems.
So.
